name: Daily Mail cryptic crossword, book 2 No 99

book.title: Daily Mail New Cryptic Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Philosopher's team providing some food

blocks.note: a side is a sports team
belonging to Francis Bacon, the English philosopher, read as 'of Bacon'

explanation.surface: A thinker's own squad turns out to be the one bringing the snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: Philosopher's team is read as the team of Bacon, giving SIDE OF BACON; Francis Bacon was the Elizabethan philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: A side of bacon is a large cured cut from one flank of a pig, certainly an item of food.

clue.text: Get hurt having to hold up among dozens of deciders

blocks.note: to sustain is to support or hold up
among means in the midst of
a jury is a panel of twelve who decide a verdict, so several of them are dozens of deciders

explanation.surface: Someone is injured trying to stall proceedings among a crowd of jurors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' looks like a container signal, but here it simply supplies a short word of its own between the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain injuries is the standard phrase for suffering wounds or damage in an accident.

clue.text: Healer with a side that's attractive

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
taken as written
a wing is a side of a building or a team

explanation.surface: A doctor with a particular flank or ward that people find appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing is an adjective here, as in a drawing card: something that pulls people in or attracts them.

clue.text: Away with nearly everything cut from the carcass

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: off means away, as in 'be off'
all means everything

explanation.surface: A butcher takes away nearly every part of the slaughtered animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the entrails and organs removed from a slaughtered animal's carcass by the butcher.

clue.text: Support quiet deal worked out in retreat

indicators.note: something worked out has been reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to back is to support
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quiet agreement is reached that lets someone back down.
explanation.definitionFit: To backpedal is to reverse a stated position, a retreat from an earlier claim or commitment.

clue.text: Occupation for a visitor

blocks.note: first meaning: a vocation or profession
second meaning: what a visitor is doing when paying a call

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one job description, but splits into a profession and the act of paying a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling is a vocation or trade, and someone calling on you is making a social visit.

clue.text: Met here with fresh country measure

blocks.note: fresh means new
a country of the United Kingdom
a yard is a unit of length

explanation.surface: We met at this spot with a newly measured country lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' is not the past of meet but the Met, London's Metropolitan Police, whose headquarters is New Scotland Yard.
explanation.definitionFit: New Scotland Yard is the headquarters building of London's Metropolitan Police, known as the Met.

clue.text: No arrogance arises when one's an inventor

indicators.note: in a down clue something that arises is read from the bottom upwards, turning it round

blocks.note: taken as written
side is an old word for swagger or putting on airs

explanation.surface: A modest person is credited as a creator with no conceit at all.
explanation.walkthrough: NO SIDE read upwards gives EDISON; 'side' meaning pretentiousness is a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the prolific American inventor of the phonograph and a practical electric light bulb.

clue.text: Catholic held up by goddess in emergency

indicators.note: held up in a down clue means lifted so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: RC is Roman Catholic
Isis was an Egyptian goddess

explanation.surface: A Catholic is delayed by a goddess at a moment of urgent need.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of acute danger or difficulty, an emergency requiring immediate action.

clue.text: Fad and fits of the female sort

indicators.note: fits suggests spasms or convulsions, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, while also signalling the mix

explanation.surface: Crazes and tantrums are presented as typically feminine traits.
explanation.walkthrough: FAD + FITS rearranged gives DISTAFF; 'fits' does double duty as both fodder and indicator. 'and' simply joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The distaff side is the female line of a family, from the spinning staff traditionally used by women.

clue.text: Struggle to avoid getting too heated?

definitions.text: Struggle to avoid getting too heated?

blocks.clueFragment: Struggle to avoid getting too heated?
blocks.note: surface reading: an effort to stop an argument boiling over
setter's reading: a conflict kept short of actual fighting, a hot war

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like keeping your temper; it actually describes a conflict that never turned into open fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: The East-West rivalry after 1945 was a hostile standoff short of direct military combat between superpowers.

clue.text: Transport for beastly couples

blocks.note: surface reading: unpleasant pairs of people being moved somewhere
setter's reading: the vessel that carried animals two by two in Genesis

explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' looks like an insult but means made of beasts: the animals boarded Noah's vessel in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah built the ark to carry pairs of every animal through the biblical flood.

clue.text: Resort to a different line for the dog

indicators.note: turned to a different form, the following word has its letters put in another order

blocks.note: a spa is a health resort
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone switches to another railway line to take the dog on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is a breed of gundog with long drooping ears and a silky coat.

clue.text: What people pay to hold name of superior people

indicators.note: one thing made to hold another keeps it inside, so a letter is placed within

blocks.note: prices are what people pay for goods
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: The cost of things is said to preserve the reputation of the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: Princes are royal sons or rulers, ranked above ordinary people in social standing.

clue.text: One whose life is in order

definitions.text: One whose life is in order

blocks.clueFragment: One whose life is in order
blocks.note: surface reading: a tidy, well-organised person
setter's reading: someone who lives within a religious order

explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' suggests neatness, but the order is a religious community of sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a woman who has taken vows and lives as a member of a religious order.

clue.text: A lot of money for a piano

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for a thousand pounds or dollars
second meaning: the large concert instrument with a horizontal frame

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as paying a fortune for an instrument; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is slang for a thousand pounds, and a grand piano is the large horizontal concert type.

clue.text: Hit Pat any way that shows dislike

indicators.note: arranged any way at all, the preceding letters can be put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, also part of the signal

explanation.surface: Striking someone called Pat by whatever means is a clear sign of hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipathy is a deep-seated aversion or hostility felt towards someone or something.

clue.text: Openings for a top person leaving Tyneside

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so that part is taken away from the word

blocks.note: a town on the south bank of the Tyne opposite Newcastle
a head is the person in charge

explanation.surface: Opportunities arise when a senior figure departs north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town on Tyneside in north-east England; remove HEAD and GATES remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Gates are hinged barriers that open to let people through, so they are openings in walls or fences.

clue.text: It's quite normal to include a singer

indicators.note: the phrase is said to include the target, which sits inside its run of letters

blocks.note: letters running across the junction of the two words

explanation.surface: It is perfectly ordinary for a vocalist to be part of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with the highest ordinary adult male voice range.

clue.text: Nota straight artist?

blocks.note: surface reading: a painter who is crooked or dishonest
setter's reading: someone who turns things round, who is also the painter of seascapes

explanation.walkthrough: The book prints Nota for Not a. J. M. W. Turner was the great English painter; a turner also turns wood on a lathe, never going straight.
explanation.definitionFit: The English Romantic painter J. M. W. Turner shares a name with a lathe worker who shapes things by rotating them.

clue.text: Colourful cover for Communist boss?

blocks.note: setter's reading: a vivid shock of hair covering someone's scalp
surface reading: the leader of a left-wing party, wittily read word by word

explanation.walkthrough: A Communist is a Red and a boss is a head, so the leader becomes a person with vividly coloured hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A redhead is a person whose hair is ginger or auburn, a colourful covering for the scalp.

clue.text: What might be told of good man's return full of drink

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the abbreviation is read backwards
something full of a substance has it inside, so one piece is put within the other

blocks.note: ST is saint, a good man
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Stories might be told of a holy man coming back home drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tales are stories, which are things told or narrated to listeners.

clue.text: No glass broken when rallying cries are made

indicators.note: something broken is shattered and its pieces lie in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Protesters promise no windows will be smashed while they chant at a rally.
explanation.definitionFit: Slogans are short memorable phrases used as watchwords to rally support for a cause.

clue.text: It may be taken with a strike in mind

definitions.text: It may be taken with a strike in mind

blocks.note: surface reading: something done when planning industrial action
setter's reading: what a marksman takes before trying to hit a target

explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests a walkout, but here it is a blow or shot hitting a target.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking aim means pointing a weapon at a target before firing or striking at it.

clue.text: Not one of the more sensible dyes?

definitions.text: Not one of the more sensible
definitions.note: an adjective phrase; the answer here is the comparative adjective
plural, while the answer names one dye plant

blocks.clueFragment: Not one of the more sensible
blocks.note: first meaning: crazier, the comparative of an adjective for insane
second meaning: a plant whose root yields a red dye

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one sentence about dyes; it is really two senses of one word joined together.
explanation.definitionFit: Madder is a plant whose root gives a red colouring, and also the comparative of mad, meaning crazier.

clue.text: Driving together when a spell of fighting is finished

blocks.note: a round is a period of a boxing bout
up means over, as in 'time's up'

explanation.surface: A cattle drive starts as soon as the bout of brawling is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A round-up is the gathering together of cattle by herding them into one place.

clue.text: Visibility impaired with old Duce on the move

indicators.note: letters that are on the move shift about and settle in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; Il Duce was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: Mussolini on the march leaves everything hazy and hard to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouded describes something obscured or made murky, so seeing through it is harder.

clue.text: No corn for goat island

indicators.note: no means without, so that word is removed from the longer one

blocks.note: the zodiac sign of the goat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A goat gets no grain on its little island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is the link between the wordplay and the definition, and 'goat' points to the star sign Capricorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples, off the coast of southern Italy.

clue.text: Muslim chief to do the cooking

blocks.note: first meaning: a military commander in the Ottoman Empire
second meaning: the heavy range cooker found in many British kitchens

explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a cast-iron range cooker, a fixture of British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga was an Ottoman commander, and an Aga is a large stove used for cooking.

clue.text: Happening to conceal identity that's obvious

indicators.note: something concealed is hidden inside, so the second piece goes within the first

blocks.note: an event is a happening
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: An incident designed to hide someone's identity is transparently obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means plainly seen or understood, clear to anyone, much the same as obvious.

clue.text: Bill taking round food to satisfy

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the short word is read backwards
one piece taking in another holds it inside

blocks.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a plate is a dish of food served at a meal

explanation.surface: A man called Bill brings food around to keep everyone happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is an account; turned round it sits inside PLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate is to soothe and pacify someone, satisfying their grievance or anger.

clue.text: Sorry not to have hit the departed loved one

blocks.note: first meaning: regretfully failed to strike the target
second meaning: the phrase used on gravestones and in death notices

explanation.walkthrough: The literal sense of an unlucky shot is combined with a phrase from obituaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadly missed is the stock tribute in death notices for someone who has died and is mourned.
